tts_summary:
Good morning. Let's get you up to speed for Monday September 21st.

Futures are rallying to kick off the week. S&P is up 49 points, about 65 basis points. Nasdaq is leading, up 110 basis points. Russell 2000 is up about 47 basis points. Asia finished broadly higher, with Korea up 165 basis points and Hong Kong up 118 basis points. Europe is up 85 to 120 basis points with data center infrastructure stocks outperforming. Treasuries have a bid, with yields down 2 to 3 basis points across the curve.

Here's what makes this rally confounding: nearly every headline from the weekend was negative. The Houthis dramatically escalated missile and drone attacks on Saudi Arabia. Ukraine launched its largest drone strike of the war against Russia, hitting an oil refinery near Moscow. And after Friday's close, a flood of troubling AI headlines landed — the Anthropic IPO is delayed, their 2027 revenue projections underwhelmed, OpenAI is projecting roughly 280 billion dollars in negative free cash flow through 2030, and Oracle's Project Jupiter data center in New Mexico is having serious trouble offloading loans tied to the facility.

So why are markets up? One word: diplomacy. The UN General Assembly opens in New York this week and runs through September 28th. Trump has signaled openness to meeting Iran's president, who is expected to attend. The bull case here is simple but powerful — if even a tiny amount of geopolitical progress is made, oil could drop sharply, and lower oil unlocks a cascade of positive macro effects: lower yields, less hawkish monetary policy, better margins, stronger consumer confidence. That is the trade the market is betting on this morning.

On the Fed and rates — the policy backdrop remains hawkish. The market is pricing about 33 basis points of additional hikes over the year's final two meetings, with roughly 50-50 odds of a move at the October 28th meeting. Both Kansas City Fed President Schmid and Minneapolis Fed President Kashkari made hawkish remarks over the weekend, warning inflation is broad-based and not just an energy story. Treasury is also planning to issue over one trillion dollars in T-bills over the next 12 months, pushing short-term debt above 24 percent of marketable debt and above their stated target.

On individual names — Oracle is under pressure after an FT report detailed serious stress in debt tied to its massive New Mexico data center. Novo Nordisk is falling in Europe after disappointing investors at its analyst day by failing to provide specific financial targets. Disney's parks business is a rare bright spot, outperforming peers through pricing promotions. Paramount and Warner are in advanced settlement talks with California's attorney general over their merger, with potential divestitures of Comedy Central on the table — outcome remains uncertain.

For the week, the big catalysts are the Trump and Xi summit on Thursday, the September flash PMIs on Wednesday morning, and any Iran diplomacy developments at the UN General Assembly. COST reports Thursday night and is the marquee earnings event of the week.

Bottom line: the directional lean today is cautiously optimistic but fragile. The rally is built on hope, not fundamentals. If diplomatic signals from the UN disappoint, this morning's gains will evaporate quickly. Watch oil. Watch headlines out of New York. That is what drives everything else right now.
